item.title: Indiana appeals court revises child support, awards father $15,275 and restores mother's obligation
item.description: In a recent case, a father requested modifications to his child support payments after both daughters moved in with him. This resulted in financial arguments and disputes over parenting-time credits involving their mother. The Indiana Court of Appeals intervened, rectifying the original court's miscalculations of the father's overpayment. The court underscored that even if children are estranged, the duty to provide support remains.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: NFL Hall of Famer Fran Tarkenton buys $51.89 million Palm Beach mansion; sellers had paid $12.65 million in 2019
item.description: Fran Tarkenton, the legendary NFL quarterback, has made headlines by acquiring a beautifully renovated Mediterranean mansion in Palm Beach for $51.89 million. This stunning property boasts five spacious bedrooms and breathtaking ocean views, complemented by exclusive beach access. Having spent considerable time in the Palm Beach area, Tarkenton now joins a select group of affluent buyers captivated by the island's luxurious real estate offerings.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Scientists scooped 11 endangered alpine spiny crayfish from a Victorian creek after bushfires
item.description: In January 2026, bushfires in Victoria threatened the alpine spiny crayfish, prompting a rescue effort by scientists. The 11 crayfish were taken to Snobs Creek conservation hatchery to recover after being rescued from dangerous waters. They faced various challenges in captivity, such as aggression towards each other, requiring individual care plans. As scientists monitor the waterways, future conservation efforts may include captive breeding programs for the species.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: When people entered a cave in Chiapas, Mexico, in 2012, they found 165 human skulls
item.description: In a remarkable discovery, a total of 165 human skulls was unearthed in a cave located in Chiapas, Mexico, shedding light on ancient Mesoamerican rituals. Dating back around 1,000 years to the Early Postclassic period, these remains included notably women and children. The research indicates that the cave could have served as a pilgrimage site, reflecting a sophisticated system of rituals connected to ancient Maya beliefs regarding the human body.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Wisconsin court upholds contempt finding against brother in family trust dispute over missing documents
item.description: In a contentious family trust dispute in Wisconsin, Todd A Mackoway was found in contempt by the court. His sister, Anne M Bartnik, pushed for his removal as trustee, claiming he neglected his duties. Mackoway's failure to provide requested financial documents and his attempts to challenge Bartnik's legal representation contributed to the court's decision, which was ultimately upheld by the appeals court, emphasizing the importance of complying with discovery requests.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Teenager built homemade radar to find buried bulls on grandfather’s farm; now Australian ‘Grave Hunter’ has uncovered more than 600 lost graves
item.description: Known for his remarkable work, Dave Hunter—'Dave the Grave Hunter'—has made a significant discovery of 658 unmarked graves throughout Australia. His company, Hunter Geophysics, employed ground-penetrating radar to meticulously complete the project in 2026, all while maintaining the integrity of existing cemeteries. Local councils are keen to safeguard these findings and attach stories to each grave. Future endeavors may also reach out to nearby areas grappling with identical predicaments.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Connecticut teacher sues school district over First Amendment rights after crucifix suspension
item.description: A Connecticut teacher was suspended after refusing to remove a crucifix she had displayed in her classroom for 10 years. She has sued the school district, alleging a violation of her First Amendment rights. An appeals court is now examining whether the crucifix constituted the teacher's private religious expression or school-related speech.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pacific survey finds 15 breeding seabird species, 132 turtle nests and two unusual fish observations
item.description: Researchers have unveiled the rich marine biodiversity of the isolated atolls of Bikar and Bokak in the Marshall Islands. Their exploration discovered robust populations of seabirds and active green sea turtle nesting grounds. Additionally, they identified a wide range of fish species across reef and deep-sea environments, including possible new species.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Bat Skulls Shrink Over Decades: Malagasy flying fox skulls are 6% smaller; commercial hunting may contribute
item.description: Studies show that the skulls of Malagasy flying foxes have become about six percent smaller over the past few decades. This reduction in size is likely attributed to factors such as commercial hunting and habitat loss due to deforestation. The decrease in larger individuals poses a threat to their reproductive success and population recovery.

item.title: Family Dollar agrees to $63 million overpricing settlement
item.description: Family Dollar is on the brink of finalizing a substantial $63 million settlement following customer allegations of price inconsistencies. Shoppers reported being charged higher amounts at the register than what was displayed in stores and online. The agreement proposes $40 million for customer refunds and another $20 million in discounts. Additionally, a new program will be initiated to uphold pricing precision in all locations, pending judicial approval from the U.S.
